clue.text: Prom starting with mass dance

indicators.note: the walk begins with the mass, so that piece is placed first

parts.note: a cake is a compacted mass or block, as in a cake of soap
a prom (promenade) is a walk

explanation.surface: A dance at the Proms opens with a performance of a Mass.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Prom' suggests the Proms concerts and 'mass' a choral Mass; here they are a walk and a cake. A CAKEWALK is a strutting dance of the late nineteenth century.
explanation.definitionFit: The cakewalk is a high-stepping dance that originated among African Americans and became a ballroom craze.

clue.text: But surely Leicester isn't so inferior?

definitions.text: But surely Leicester isn't so inferior?

parts.words: But surely Leicester isn't so inferior?
parts.note: Red Leicester is a British cheese, so the question plays on a word meaning cheap and inferior that also means like cheese

explanation.definitionFit: Cheesy means cheap, tacky and of poor quality, as well as tasting of cheese.

clue.text: Ring for the custodian

definitions.meaning: a guard ring worn to stop another ring slipping off the finger
a guardian or warden in charge of something

explanation.definitionFit: A keeper ring guards a wedding ring, and a keeper is a custodian or warden.

clue.text: Carouser lived on boat

parts.note: was means existed or lived
a sailer is a vessel described by how it sails, as in a good sailer

explanation.surface: A heavy drinker spent his life aboard a ship.
explanation.definitionFit: A wassailer is a reveller who drinks healths at a festive party, a carouser.

clue.text: Tall equestrian raises son to be docker

parts.note: long means tall

indicators.note: in a down answer the son's letter is lifted higher up the word

parts.note: a horseman is an equestrian

explanation.surface: A tall rider brings up his boy to work at the docks.
explanation.walkthrough: 'raises' lifts the S of HORSEMAN to the top, giving SHOREMAN.
explanation.definitionFit: A longshoreman is a dock labourer who loads and unloads ships, a docker.

clue.text: Anticlimax, finding duck in public pool

indicators.note: the duck is placed inside the public pool

parts.note: public baths are a municipal swimming pool
a duck is a score of nothing in cricket, so O

explanation.surface: Someone is disappointed to find a duck swimming in the local pool.
explanation.definitionFit: Bathos is an abrupt and ludicrous descent from the elevated to the trivial, a literary anticlimax.

clue.text: Evil intent abandoned by married woman

indicators.note: the married letter leaves the word for evil intent

parts.note: malice is the intention to do harm

explanation.surface: A wife gives up her spiteful plans.
explanation.definitionFit: Alice is a woman's name, used here as an example of a woman.

clue.text: Type of crack hostess originally employed by flight operator

indicators.note: only the opening letter of hostess is used

parts.note: an airline operates flights

explanation.surface: An air hostess is taken on by a carrier.
explanation.walkthrough: 'employed by' only joins: the hostess's initial stands with the airline that employs her.
explanation.definitionFit: A hairline crack is a very thin fracture, so hairline names a type of crack.

clue.text: Hoarder runs into landowner on lake

indicators.note: the runs letter goes inside the landowner

parts.note: a squire is a country landowner
R is the cricket abbreviation for runs

explanation.surface: A collector bumps into the lord of the manor beside the lake.
explanation.definitionFit: A squirrel stores nuts for winter, so the word is used of anyone who hoards.

clue.text: Nevertheless, new gillies initially give service

parts.note: even so means nevertheless

indicators.note: only the first letter of gillies is wanted

explanation.surface: Despite everything, the new Highland hunting attendants begin by attending church.
explanation.walkthrough: Gillies are attendants on a Scottish hunting or fishing estate.
explanation.definitionFit: Evensong is the Anglican evening prayer service, so it is a church service.

clue.text: I recline in a Greek character's environment

indicators.note: I and recline go inside the Greek character

parts.note: mu is a letter of the Greek alphabet; the 's links it to the definition
to lie is to recline

explanation.surface: Someone lounges on a couch in a setting fit for a classical Greek.
explanation.definitionFit: A milieu is a person's social surroundings, a synonym for environment or setting.

clue.text: Briefly, several old fellows involved in president's music

indicators.note: the word for several is cut short by its last letter

parts.note: divers is an archaic word for several

indicators.note: the fellows are wrapped inside the president

parts.note: Tito was president of Yugoslavia
men are fellows

explanation.surface: In short, a group of elderly men take part in a president's concert.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Briefly' trims DIVERS to DIVER; 'involved in' puts MEN inside TITO.
explanation.definitionFit: A divertimento is a light instrumental piece, chiefly of the eighteenth century.

clue.text: Female graduate in land of noted royal arrival

parts.note: she is the female pronoun
a BA, Bachelor of Arts, is a graduate

explanation.surface: A woman with a degree lives in a famous kingdom.
explanation.walkthrough: The royal arrival is the Queen of Sheba, who visited King Solomon in the Bible.
explanation.definitionFit: Sheba was the biblical kingdom whose queen famously arrived at Solomon's court.

clue.text: One whinges when dealer keeps French wine back

indicators.note: the dealer holds the reversed wine within it

parts.note: a seller is a dealer

indicators.note: the French word for wine is read backwards

parts.note: vin is French for wine

explanation.surface: A whining customer complains when the merchant holds back French wine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back' turns VIN into NIV, which 'keeps' puts inside SELLER.
explanation.definitionFit: A sniveller is someone who whines and complains tearfully, a whinger.

clue.text: University surrounded by blooming radiation!

indicators.note: the university letter is enclosed by the word for blooming

parts.note: florescence is the process or state of flowering

explanation.surface: A university campus is ringed by flowers giving off an alarming glow.
explanation.definitionFit: Fluorescence is light emitted by a substance absorbing radiation, a form of radiation itself.

clue.text: Train 11, for example, to make vehicle body

parts.note: to coach is to train
the answer to 11 down is a musical composition, an example of a work

explanation.surface: Coaching a team of eleven builds the body of a vehicle.
explanation.walkthrough: The cross-reference points to 11 down, a piece of music, which is a work.
explanation.definitionFit: Coachwork is the bodywork of a road or rail vehicle.

clue.text: Element Kentish chap identified at first with hesitation

parts.note: Kent is in the south-east of England, SE
Len is a man's name, standing for any chap

indicators.note: only the first letter of identified is wanted

parts.note: um is a hesitant sound

explanation.surface: A man from Kent is recognised only after some hesitation.
explanation.walkthrough: Kent is a county in south-east England, so Kentish gives SE.
explanation.definitionFit: Selenium is a chemical element, number 34, a non-metal.

clue.text: Receptacle PM carried in withou delay

indicators.note: the prime minister is held inside the word for without delay

parts.note: soon means without delay; the paper printed withou, a typo for without
Pitt was a British Prime Minister

explanation.surface: The Prime Minister is quickly brought in on a container.
explanation.walkthrough: The paper prints 'withou', a typo for 'without'. PM is Prime Minister; both William Pitts held that office.
explanation.definitionFit: A spittoon is a receptacle for spitting into.

clue.text: Old fairy in tale oddly derived from personal observation

parts.note: ex means former or old
a peri is a fairy in Persian mythology

indicators.note: the letters of in tale are arranged in an odd, unusual way

explanation.surface: An old fairy appears in a strange story drawn from someone's own experience.
explanation.walkthrough: 'oddly' rearranges IN TALE into ENTIAL; it does not mean taking odd letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Experiential means based on experience, that is, derived from personal observation.

clue.text: Eager to have paintings around study

indicators.note: the paintings go round the study

parts.note: art means paintings collectively
a den is a private study

explanation.surface: Someone keen to hang pictures all round the study.
explanation.definitionFit: Ardent means passionate and eager.

clue.text: Such a problem when granny slips?

definitions.text: Such a problem when granny slips?

parts.words: Such a problem when granny slips?
parts.note: a granny is a badly tied reef that slips, so the clue reads as a problem full of tangled ties

explanation.definitionFit: A knotty problem is one that is intricate and hard to solve.

clue.text: Place most prepared for medium production

indicators.note: the letters of place most are made ready in a new arrangement

explanation.surface: A venue is got ready for a spiritualist medium's performance.
explanation.definitionFit: Ectoplasm is the substance supposedly exuded by a spiritualist medium during a seance.

clue.text: Archbishop? Not at first

indicators.note: the word at is not wanted, so it is removed

parts.note: a primate is an archbishop

explanation.surface: Asks whether someone is an archbishop, but not to begin with.
explanation.walkthrough: 'first' wants to be part of 'at first'; it is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Prime means first in rank or importance.

clue.text: One bird or another only partly visible

indicators.note: the bird can be seen in part, spread across the words another only

explanation.surface: Birdwatchers glimpse one bird, or perhaps another half-hidden.
explanation.definitionFit: The heron is a long-legged wading bird of rivers and marshes.

clue.text: Current section following conventional type

parts.note: I is the symbol for electric current
a conic is a conic section, the curve cut from a cone

explanation.surface: An up-to-date section follows the standard pattern.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Current' looks like 'modern' but it is I, the physics symbol.
explanation.definitionFit: In art, iconic describes figures following a fixed conventional type, as in religious images.

clue.text: Popular hand-out — books for the workshy

parts.note: in means fashionable or popular
the dole is state unemployment benefit, a handout
NT, the New Testament, is a collection of books

explanation.surface: Popular benefit payments and reading matter for the idle.
explanation.walkthrough: The DOLE is the everyday British name for unemployment benefit.
explanation.definitionFit: Indolent means lazy and averse to effort, the same as workshy.

clue.text: £500, or a thousand in cash

indicators.note: the thousand is put inside the cash

parts.note: money is cash
K stands for a thousand, from kilo

explanation.surface: A sum offered either as five hundred pounds or a thousand in notes.
explanation.walkthrough: MONKEY is British slang for five hundred pounds.
explanation.definitionFit: In British slang a monkey is five hundred pounds sterling.

clue.text: Science Tsiolkovsky initiated in part of garden?

indicators.note: the initial goes inside the garden feature

parts.note: a rockery is a garden area of rocks and plants

indicators.note: only the initial letter of Tsiolkovsky is used

explanation.surface: The rocket pioneer Tsiolkovsky started his science in a corner of the garden.
explanation.walkthrough: Konstantin Tsiolkovsky was the Russian father of rocket theory, which keeps the answer in the scene.
explanation.definitionFit: Rocketry is the science and technology of rockets.
